literature_expectation: Most adhesion, signalling or development HOGs of the multicellular clade are present at the pre-transition node; the share new at the post-transition node is not higher than at matched control nodes
source: Sebé-Pedrós et al. 2017; Brunet & King 2017; Glöckner et al. 2016; Kiss et al. 2019; Prochnik et al. 2010; Sheikh et al. 2024
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 H1/H2 primary (sequence-novel gains vs matched controls) with co-option index 4.3
outcome: supported (descriptive; comparative part not detected at this power)
our_evidence: Co-option index 0.80-1.00: 80-100% of expanded Pfam families present at P in all 7 transitions; presence controls C04/C05/C09/C11 recovered; but Metazoa (0.80) and Streptophyta (0.83) below all 20 matched controls (u=0.024; Pfam-only, HOG version no effect); stem novelty excess not detected (H1/H2 p=0.113)

literature_expectation: Gains per unit branch length at transition nodes exceed the control distribution; the burst should survive rarefaction of the outgroups (Richter et al. 2018 shows it may not)
source: Paps & Holland 2018; Bowles et al. 2020; Denoeud et al. 2024
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 H1/H2 primary; rarefaction DESIGN 4.4
our_evidence: H1/H2 T=0.711, parametric-bootstrap p=0.113, Holm p=0.452; pooled O/E 1.67 [0.64, 4.34] (MDE 2.4-5.9-fold); below the 2.2-fold Dev-4 method-bias threshold; per stem Metazoa 594 vs 247 predicted (u=0.83), Streptophyta 189 vs 178; rarefaction not run

literature_expectation: Clades that later transition have outgroup ancestors with more adhesion/TF/signalling HOGs than sister clades that never transitioned
source: Ocaña-Pallarès et al. 2022; Grau-Bové et al. 2017; Merényi et al. 2020
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 secondary/exploratory (BH within exploratory family)
our_evidence: Not run (pre-transition accumulation on outgroup ancestors was not analysed)

literature_expectation: Duplication rates within TF HOGs (Pfam DNA-binding domains) are higher on transition branches than on control branches
source: de Mendoza et al. 2013; Larroux et al. 2008; Lang et al. 2010; Catarino et al. 2016; Knoll 2011
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 H4 primary (share of stem duplications in TF-DBD HOGs; C2H2 excluded)
our_evidence: H4 T=0.548, p=0.361, Holm p=0.808; pooled odds ratio 1.16 [0.62, 2.19] (MDE 2.8); orthology-free p=0.184; duplication re-placement p=0.527; Metazoa extreme only after re-placement (TF-DBD dups 21->30, u 0.64->0.98)

literature_expectation: The TF effect is greater for complex (X) than simple (S) transitions
source: Knoll 2011; de Mendoza et al. 2013
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 H4 (complex x transition interaction, estimate only; low power with ~6 S->X transitions)
our_evidence: Only Metazoa is complex among primary stems (u=0.64); nested complex secondary set H4 p=0.687, pooled odds ratio 0.98 [0.40, 2.37]; complex x transition interaction not estimated

literature_expectation: Zn-cluster TF change at yeast reversals (Nagy et al. 2014; re-attributed from transitions to reversals in evo_biology.md 5)
source: Nagy et al. 2014
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 reversal analysis (exploratory)
our_evidence: Zn-cluster TF dynamics at yeast reversals not analysed; reversal analysis covered gained/duplicated HOGs only

literature_expectation: The same Pfam domain classes (cadherin-like, lectin, fibronectin-like, Ig-like, LRR, EGF-like) expand independently in >=2 lineages more often than in a permutation null over control nodes
source: Knoll 2011; Abedin & King 2010; Pereira Lobo et al. 2025; Rokas 2008a
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 H5 primary (adhesion_ecm and signalling classes; immune LRR excluded)
our_evidence: H5 T=0.412, p=0.772, Holm p=0.808; pooled odds ratio 0.83 [0.55, 1.27] (MDE 2.2; CI excludes 1.5-fold expansion but not 1.5-fold depletion); orthology-free p=0.421 with opposite sign; Pfam-wide convergent expansion 370 vs 643 expected (p=0.79), top domains transposon-derived

literature_expectation: Protein kinase HOGs with transmembrane or extracellular domains duplicate on the brown algal, streptophyte and holozoan/animal branches
source: Cock et al. 2010; Shiu & Bleecker 2001; Manning et al. 2008
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 secondary/exploratory (kinase classification beyond PF07714; toolkit_pfam.tsv)
our_evidence: Receptor-kinase (TM/extracellular) classification beyond the toolkit classes not run

scope: all primary transitions (fungal hyphae stem as null)
literature_expectation: No receptor-kinase HOG duplication expansion on the fungal hyphae branch
source: Kiss et al. 2019
our_test: DESIGN 6 positive control C15 (expected null); H6 exploratory
our_evidence: Positive control C15 recovered: fungal-hyphae path stem shows no expansion of kinase_ptyr (odds ratio 1.39, u=0.74), adhesion/ECM (0.69, u=0.26) or signalling (0.50, u=0.41) vs 20 matched controls

literature_expectation: HOGs gained at aggregative nodes (Dictyostelia, Acrasidae, Fonticula, Copromyxa, Guttulinopsis, Myxococcota) are enriched for signal peptides and transmembrane proteins compared with gains at control nodes
source: Glöckner et al. 2016
our_test: DESIGN 3.3 and 4.2 exploratory (TM/SP predictor)
our_evidence: Signal-peptide/transmembrane predictor not run; Dictyostelia PKS expansion (control C16: median 16 vs 1 proteins per species) recovered but is not the H7 test

literature_expectation: Aggregative myxobacterial transition (Myxococcota) shows enrichment of signal-peptide/TM gains relative to controls
source: Glöckner et al. 2016
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 exploratory; prokaryote run (DESIGN 3.1)
our_evidence: Signal-peptide/transmembrane predictor not run; prokaryotes descriptive only (|U|=2)

literature_expectation: Gene content turnover (gains + duplications) at clonal nodes exceeds that at aggregative nodes after correcting for branch length and sampling
source: Grosberg & Strathmann 2007; Fisher et al. 2013; Márquez-Zacarías et al. 2021
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 exploratory (demoted; matched contrasts only; aggregative cases mostly single-species)
our_evidence: Clonal vs aggregative turnover contrast not run (one aggregative primary transition, Dictyostelia)

literature_expectation: After transitions in eukaryotes: longer proteins, more disorder, more multidomain proteins, more HOGs, and higher genome-wide relative rates
source: Lynch & Conery 2003; Lynch 2007; Bingham & Ratcliff 2024; Pentz et al. 2023
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 H9 primary; 4.5 relative-rate test and protein traits on shared single-copy HOGs
our_evidence: H9 pooled rate ratio 1.10 [0.96, 1.26], p=0.269, Holm p=0.808: no >=1.5-fold genome-wide rate shift (MDE 1.26-1.69); 4 stems faster, 3 slower; RER 0 genes at q<0.10; Kr/Kc charge p=0.60, polarity p=0.16; disorder/length shifts not distinct from controls (u 0.34-0.82)

literature_expectation: In prokaryotes: no increase, or a decrease, in gene count at transitions; direction is opposite to eukaryotes
source: Lynch 2007; Bingham & Ratcliff 2024
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 secondary/exploratory (prokaryote gene-count side of H9; prokaryote run)
our_evidence: Descriptive only (|U|=2): losses exceed HOG gains on all 4 stems (e.g. Streptomycetaceae 301 gains vs 4,723 losses) but also on both control branches; rate ratios 0.72-1.47

literature_expectation: Disorder fraction in TF HOGs correlates with cell-type number under phylogenetic regression and increases on transition branches compared with orthologous HOGs on control branches
source: Schad et al. 2011; Yruela et al. 2017; Chen et al. 2014; Dunker et al. 2015
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 secondary/exploratory; 4.5 protein traits
our_evidence: Exploratory: disorder on shared single-copy HOGs rises in 4/7 transitions (+0.019 to +0.037) and falls in volvocines/Metazoa; percentiles vs controls 0.34-0.73; phylogenetic regression on cell-type number not run

literature_expectation: The rate of new domain architectures per HOG is higher on Metazoa, brown algal, streptophyte and Agaricomycetes branches than on control branches
source: Ekman et al. 2007; Denoeud et al. 2024; Ocaña-Pallarès et al. 2022
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 secondary/exploratory; architecture-novel gains (DESIGN 3.2 tier 4)
our_evidence: New multi-domain architectures on stems T=0.80, p=0.005 (7 primary stems; exploratory); Metazoa 1,131 vs matched-control median 34 (u=0.98), Streptophyta u=0.88, PX u=0.83; survives leave-one-out (p<=0.017) and genome-only; fails BUSCO>=80% filter (p=0.16); pooled O/E 1.02 [0.36, 2.91]; Agaricomycetes not tested

literature_expectation: HOGs lost at transition nodes are enriched for motility (flagellar) and phagotrophy functions (direction pre-registered per transition in h12_expected_direction.tsv)
source: Merényi et al. 2023; Yang et al. 2026; Nguyen et al. 2017
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 H12 primary (flagellar-module losses; concordance count vs relabelling)
our_evidence: H12 T=0.738, p=0.020, Holm p=0.102; both loss-expected stems (fungal hyphae, Dictyostelia) lose all 4 flagellar modules, others 0-16%; power <=0.33 even with complete loss; exploratory convergent domain loss reduces to the same fungi x Dictyostelia flagellar loss (cilium domains OR 17)

literature_expectation: At reversals, HOGs gained at the earlier transition are lost preferentially
source: Merényi et al. 2023; Nguyen et al. 2017
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 exploratory reversals
our_evidence: Exploratory: odds of losing HOGs gained/duplicated at the preceding transition 0.86-1.39 in 6 reversals (5 yeasts, Zygnematophyceae); relative to multicellular sisters 0.32-1.21 (<1 in 5 of 6)

literature_expectation: At reversals to unicellularity (unicellular cyanobacteria), HOGs gained at the earlier transition are lost preferentially (testable only in the prokaryote run)
source: Yang et al. 2026
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 exploratory; prokaryote run
our_evidence: Only pseudo-reversals (unicellular cyanobacterial clades) run as a pipeline demonstration; no real prokaryotic reversal tested

literature_expectation: RB/E2F, ubiquitin-proteasome and ESCRT/septin HOGs show duplications or accelerated relative rates on clonal transition branches (RB is a co-option control in volvocines, not a duplication prediction: evo_biology.md 5)
source: Hanschen et al. 2016; Featherston et al. 2018; Chaigne & Brunet 2022
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 secondary/exploratory; cell_cycle toolkit category; control C11
our_evidence: Not tested as specified; control C11 recovered (RB pathway present at the unicellular volvocine ancestor, consistent with co-option)

literature_expectation: No such duplications or rate acceleration on aggregative branches
source: Hanschen et al. 2016; Featherston et al. 2018; Chaigne & Brunet 2022
our_test: DESIGN 4.2 secondary/exploratory (clonal vs aggregative contrast)
our_evidence: Clonal vs aggregative contrast not run
